chunks: And from him, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sulayman ibn Khalid and Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibn Muskan, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who performed Tamattu' and did not find a sacrificial animal. He said, 'He should fast for three days.' I said to him, 'Are these from the Days of Tashriq?' He said, 'No, but he should remain in Mecca until he fasts them, and seven [days] when he returns to his people. If his companions do not stay with him and he is unable to remain in Mecca, let him fast ten days when he returns to his people.' Then he mentioned the hadith of Budayl ibn Warqa'.
And from him, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'Ibn al-Sarraj mentioned that he wrote to you asking you about a person performing Tamattu' who did not have a sacrificial animal, so you answered in your letter that he should fast three days in Mina. If he misses that, he should fast on the morning of al-Hsabah and two days after that.' He said, 'As for the days of Mina, they are days of eating and drinking; there is no fasting in them. And seven days when he returns to his people.'

key_terms.أَيَّامُ التَّشْرِيقِ: Days of Tashriq (11th, 12th, and 13th of Dhu al-Hijjah)
key_terms.تَمَتَّعَ: Performed Tamattu' (a type of Hajj combining Umrah and Hajj)
key_terms.صَبِيحَةَ الْحَصْبَةِ: The morning of al-Hsabah (the day after the 13th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a pilgrim who performs Tamattu' but cannot afford a sacrificial animal?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the fidya for a Mutamatti' pilgrim lacking a sacrificial animal, emphasizing the distinction between the 'Days of Eating and Drinking' in Mina and the specific days for fasting. The ruling prioritizes fasting three days in Mecca (excluding Tashriq) and seven upon return, offering flexibility for those unable to remain in Mecca. This reflects the Shia jurisprudential focus on the practical feasibility of expiation while maintaining the sanctity of the Hajj rituals.
